member.name: T:FMActionLink.ActionLink
member.summary: Entry point for other BepInEx plugins. Add buttons and panels from your plugin's Load() (declare [BepInDependency(Plugin.Guid)] so this plugin loads first). Everything you add shows up the next time the screen is built; nothing needs the game to restart. Callbacks run on the game's main thread: keep them short and move any I/O to Task.Run.

members.member: Sends an event to the app configured in FMActionLink.json ("app.eventsUrl"). This is what buttons and panels without their own callbacks do by default.
The buttons and panels of one game screen, in the order they were added.
Goes up on every change, so the screen watcher knows it must rebuild.
What the plugin knows about the screen when something happens.
The player's unique ID, read from the "ID: n" text in the profile header. Null when the header does not show it (see the guide: "Player ID").
A rectangle in Windows screen pixels (physical pixels, top-left origin), ready to position a window of your own.
A rectangle in Windows screen pixels (physical pixels, top-left origin), ready to position a window of your own.
Text on the button. Leave empty for an icon-only square button.
PNG file (absolute, or relative to the plugin folder). Optional.
Optional keyboard shortcut, e.g. "ctrl+shift+p". Works while the screen is open.
A plain button: one click, one action.

A button that stands for a window of your app shown over the game (a preview, a 3D view...). The plugin never draws that window: it tells you when to open, pin and close it, and where the button is, so your app positions its own window. Rules: with OpenOnHover, resting the mouse on the button opens (Hover) and leaving closes; a click pins it (Pinned) until a click elsewhere in the game, Esc, a second click on the button, or leaving the screen.
Default (null): sends "window.open" to your app.
Default (null): sends "window.pin" to your app (a hover window became pinned).
Default (null): sends "window.close" to your app.
Where the button is on screen: open your window next to it.
The game's process: hide your window whenever another process is in front.

An empty area the plugin adds to the screen, for your app to cover with a window of its own (a 3D view, a chart, an image...). The plugin keeps reporting where it is. It is placed between two text labels of the screen that sit in the same column: below the one in AfterLabel and above the one in BeforeLabel (any of the given translations).
Shown inside the area until your window covers it. Optional.
Called when the area appears, moves, changes size or shows another player, and again every 2 s while it stays still. Default (null): sends "panel.show" to your app.
Called when the area stops being visible (other tab, other screen, game minimized). Default (null): sends "panel.hide" to your app.
One message to your app, posted as JSON to "app.eventsUrl". See the guide for every event and field.

member.name: T:FMActionLink.AppLink
member.summary: Posts events to the creator's app, one at a time and in order (a "close" must never overtake the "open" before it). When a click finds the app closed and "startIfClosed" is set, starts it and keeps retrying the latest click until it answers.

member.name: T:FMActionLink.OutsideGame
member.summary: Starts programs and addresses outside the game's process group. Started directly by fm.exe they become its children, and Steam keeps showing the game as running after it closes, until those programs close too.

members.member: A program without arguments, a document or an http(s) address: the Windows shell (explorer) opens it as if the user had double-clicked it.
A program with arguments: explorer cannot pass them, so the Windows process service (WMI Win32_Process.Create) starts it; its parent is the WMI host, not the game.

Once per session: the texts that look like an ID, so a new header format can be recognised from a single log.
Looks like the game's own "Actions" button: same style classes on the button and on its text, so any skin that restyles "Actions" restyles these too.
Between the two labels, only when they are stacked in the same column. Labels side by side (the goalkeeper profile puts "Goalkeeping" in a column of its own) are skipped.
The closest element containing both, plus the child of it on the way to each.
"ctrl+shift+p", "alt+f5"... The last part is a key name from Unity's Input System.

member.name: T:FMActionLink.SharedRow
member.summary: One row next to the game's "Actions" button, shared by every plugin that adds buttons there (this one, FM ActionLink - FMSH, any other). Each plugin keeps its buttons in a group of its own inside the row; groups are named "actionlink-group-NNN-name" and always kept sorted by name, so NNN decides the order whoever loads first (FMSH is 000: always first). The row's name and the group naming are the whole agreement: plugins never reference each other, and each carries its own copy of this code.

members.member: Puts the group in the row (created right after "Actions" if missing), replacing an older group of the same name, and sorts the row.
Takes the group out, and the row with it when nobody else is left in it.
Whether this element is the row or one of its groups (never the game's "Actions").
